patient.key: BMI 43, daytime hypersomnolence despite 9h sleep, pre-bariatric clearance in 2 weeks — needs sleep study then CPAP

sequence.what: 48M BMI 43, HTN 160/90, office visit for fatigue/daytime sleepiness; bariatric surgery in 2 weeks pending clearance; GERD on pantoprazole; DOE
sequence.decision: Obesity + hypersomnolence = OSA until sleep study proves it; clearance is the clock

sequence.what: Office → continued lisinopril, atorvastatin, pantoprazole, metformin; added amlodipine; HEENT/chest/heart/abdomen largely unrevealing
sequence.decision: Normal lung/heart exam does not exclude OSA — the pathology is nocturnal airway collapse

sequence.what: CBC normal Hct; UA normal; echo mild PASP rise; facial XR normal; ENT consult no recs; A1c + insulin started; calorie-restricted diet
sequence.decision: You screened obesity comorbidities and preop labs but never ordered the cardiopulmonary sleep study

sequence.what: Patient update: proceeding to bariatric surgery; timed out without polysomnography or CPAP
sequence.decision: Case ends when CPAP is ordered after positive sleep study — without those two, score collapses

missed.why: Daytime sleepiness with 9 hours in bed in a BMI-43 man is OSA until measured. Only the sleep study diagnoses obstructive apneas; without it you cannot clear him for bariatric anesthesia safely.
Treatment that ends the case. Splints the collapsible oropharynx open at night, stops intermittent hypoxia, and is required before elective surgery in known OSA.
Documented hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin and obesity comorbidity screen before surgery — lipids are part of the metabolic package the case grades.
Laparoscopic bariatric surgery in two weeks — preop blood bank readiness is graded with the other surgical labs you already ordered (EKG, coag).
